findings.title: BRONZE SANDCASTLE deploys modified Meterpreter shells
findings.summary_md: Sophos CTU and SophosLabs describe a cluster of incidents attributed to BRONZE SANDCASTLE, a China-based group whose most distinctive marker is sideloading from legitimate Sandboxie executables and from javaw.exe through a malicious jli.dll. The sideloaded DLL reads encrypted config.ini files and decodes backdoor payloads in memory, including a modified Meterpreter shell. CTU observed victims in the Philippines, Taiwan, Afghanistan and Namibia, and likely the Republic of Korea, in incidents between August 2025 and August 2026. The report recommends behavioral detection of DLLs that read local files and immediately execute code in memory rather than static file scanning, and notes activity concentrated in UTC+8 hours.

findings.title: Operation ShadowCloud: cloud service–based backdoors targeting government networks in Asia and Africa. Part 1
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky's first installment documents an active campaign identified in early 2026 in which the legitimate MeshAgent utility is abused to drop the GitDoor and GraphDoor backdoors. The implants hide command and control in Microsoft SharePoint, GitHub and Ably, download plug-ins on demand and inject shellcode in memory. The report details loader DLLs including jli.dll and SbieDll.dll that decrypt config.ini payloads, the GitDoor protocol using GitHub issues and repositories plus rest.ably.io, and custom shellcode families often shipped as COFF objects. Kaspersky says victims were found in Asia and Africa, primarily in the government sector.

findings.title: Operation ShadowCloud: cloud service–based backdoors targeting government networks in Asia and Africa. Part 2
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky's second installment analyzes GraphDoor, identified by MD5 14ec33ea808e697870d00c5e434c2952, which opens a PID-derived named pipe and creates a GUID-named directory under C:\ProgramData\Intel_Log before harvesting system information. It documents the scr.ts, pr.ts and kl.ts plug-ins for screenshots, process listing and keylogging, plus a modified Erfrp proxy and Ably channel proxies that tunnel traffic through legitimate cloud messaging. The report notes that the backdoor obtains C2 details from proxy channels rather than hardcoded domains, and that two observed IPs resolve to twnic[.]top and ekmt[.]tw. Kaspersky reports overlaps with FamousSparrow and CopperTurtle staging on victim systems within a one-day window, while stopping short of a definitive attribution.
